clue.text: Said goodbye, embarrassed about fishy preparation

indicators.note: said tells us a word spoken aloud is wanted, written the way it sounds

parts.note: ciao is Italian for goodbye, and sounds like the start here

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for embarrassed reads backwards

parts.note: embarrassed people go red

explanation.surface: Someone says farewell, blushing over a dish of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick soup of fish or clams is a classic preparation of seafood, so fishy fits.

clue.text: Arrange overdraft provided in county's banks

indicators.note: in means placed inside the edges
the banks of something are its edges, so the outer letters are used

parts.note: OD is the banking abbreviation for overdrawn or overdraft
if means provided, as a condition

explanation.surface: Setting up an overdraft with banks in the county.
explanation.walkthrough: The banks of county are C and Y; the 's is a link meaning 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: To systematise laws or rules into a code is to arrange them in order.

clue.text: Plant publication about European duck

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the publication wraps the other letter

parts.note: an organ is a periodical or newspaper of a group
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, hence O

explanation.surface: A magazine article on European ducks and plants.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic Mediterranean herb is a plant, related to marjoram.

clue.text: Abandon reduced price for foreign jumper

parts.note: to desert is to abandon

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a rate is a price

explanation.surface: Discount clothing including a foreign sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' is not a British sweater but an animal that jumps: the jerboa.
explanation.definitionFit: The jerboa, a hopping rodent of North African deserts, bears this nickname: an animal jumper from abroad.

clue.text: Checks on small coaches

parts.note: re means on or concerning
trainers coach people

explanation.surface: Checks being made on small coaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that hold back or curb are restraints, like checks on movement.

clue.text: Hunter, swift steed, second to front

indicators.note: to front says the letter named is taken from its place and set at the start of the word

parts.note: a courser is a fast horse in poetic language

explanation.surface: A description of a huntsman on a fast horse, with a second rider coming forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to front' moves the S of COURSER from its fifth place to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: One who scours an area searches it thoroughly, so a scourer is a searcher or hunter.

clue.text: Drop one in without issue

indicators.note: in means the numeral is put inside

parts.note: s.p., Latin sine prole, means without children in genealogies
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone drops one in quietly without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means offspring, as in family trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop of liquid is a small mouthful or taste, the same sense as the noun here.

clue.text: Old book marks popping up in Vile Bodies

indicators.note: in a down clue popping up means read from bottom to top
in means the letters lie within the words given

explanation.surface: Evelyn Waugh's novel Vile Bodies has marks appearing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Daggers and similar signs were used in old manuscripts to mark doubtful passages, so they are old book marks.

clue.text: Teacher brought up possible German course

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read upwards

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
Otto is a German man's name, so an example of a German

explanation.surface: A teacher raised the possibility of a German course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a dish at a meal, not a class.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice dish served as part of a meal is one course.

clue.text: Taunt English after understandable Irish Rising

indicators.note: after means the English letter follows
in a down clue rising means read upwards

parts.note: lucid means clear and understandable

explanation.surface: English mockery following a clearly explained Irish uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish Rising' suggests the 1916 Easter Rising but 'Rising' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock or jeer at someone is to taunt them, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Makes more impressive clothes more expensive

parts.note: dresses are items of clothing
prices that are up have risen

explanation.surface: Glamorous clothes cost more than plain ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish something to look grander is idiomatically to make it fancier or smarter.

clue.text: Stopped losing head, and relaxed

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: ceased means stopped

explanation.surface: Someone stopped losing their temper and calmed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension that has slackened has been loosened, a synonym of relaxed.

clue.text: Dash just across line

indicators.note: across means the word for just straddles the other piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: fair means just

explanation.surface: A runner dashes only just across the finishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash in the sense of style or panache matches natural stylishness and verve.

clue.text: Article is worked on

definitions.note: an adjective: feasible, as in 'that plan just isn't on'

indicators.note: worked means the letters are reshaped or kneaded into a new order

explanation.surface: A news article is being worked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like part of 'worked on' but stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a plan that is on is feasible or practical, the sense of sensible and achievable.

clue.text: A good church attendance, not to do Mass

indicators.note: not means the word for swindle is taken away

parts.note: the congregation is the body of people at a church service
to con someone is to do or swindle them

explanation.surface: A decent turnout at church, not the people attending Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks religious but means a gathered whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A collected whole or accumulation of things is a mass.

clue.text: Getting on train for Eton, say

parts.note: boarding a vehicle is getting on it
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Boarding a train bound for Eton.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the famous English private school where pupils live in, an example of this kind.

clue.text: Polite tip that's given to royals

parts.note: civil means polite
to list is to tip or lean over, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A courteous tip handed to members of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the annual grant once voted by Parliament to fund the British monarch's household, money given to royals.

clue.text: One sultan resolved to capture British port

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to capture means to hold inside
resolved means broken down and reformed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sultan determined to seize a British harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' turns SULTAN into STANUL, which captures B.
explanation.definitionFit: The Turkish city on the Bosphorus, once the Ottoman capital, is a major port.

clue.text: Regular carrier beginning at Badminton?

definitions.meaning: a scheduled transport running back and forth on a set route
a game of badminton begins with someone serving the shuttlecock

explanation.surface: A bus that runs regularly starting from Badminton, the village of horse trials fame.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-and-fro scheduled transport link is one sense; striking the shuttlecock to start a rally is the other.

clue.text: Erect a pale in river in the dark

indicators.note: in means the reversed phrase is placed inside the river

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

indicators.note: in a down clue erect means set upright, so read upwards

parts.note: wan means pale

explanation.surface: An instruction to build a fence in a river at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pale' is not a fence post but an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kept in the dark idiomatically means not knowing, so uninformed.

clue.text: Bread and some butter included in tea

indicators.note: included in means put inside the word for tea

parts.note: chai is spiced Indian tea
a pat is a small portion of butter

explanation.surface: Bread and butter included in afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a flat unleavened Indian bread, an example of bread.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing ordered goods

parts.note: bade is a past tense of bid, meaning ordered
G is good, so two of them are goods

explanation.surface: A lazy person ordered goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotten person is idiomatically a worthless sort or a ne'er-do-well.

clue.text: Sick Asian nursing a broken leg brings relief

indicators.note: nursing means holding inside, as one nurses a baby in one's arms
sick means unwell or out of sorts, so these letters are disordered
broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: An ill Asian patient with a fractured leg gets pain relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick' turns ASIAN into AN...SIA, which by 'nursing' holds A plus LGE ('broken' leg).
explanation.definitionFit: Absence of feeling pain is a medical term for pain relief, so relief fits.

clue.text: Sail east then north into former colony

indicators.note: into means the compass letters travel inside the colony's name, as a ship sails into a harbour

parts.note: Goa was a Portuguese colony in India
E is the compass abbreviation for east
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Sailing east and then north towards a former colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sail' looks like a verb but names a large jib.
explanation.definitionFit: A large overlapping jib used on yachts is a type of sail.

clue.text: Fleece supplier a shopping centre rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A wool supplier was turned down by a shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American animal is kept for its woolly coat, so it supplies fleece.

clue.text: Beef not cooked in rind of bacon

indicators.note: in means the uncooked piece goes inside
the rind of something is its outside, so the outer letters are taken

parts.note: raw food is not cooked

explanation.surface: Uncooked beef wrapped in a bacon rind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' is muscle power here, not meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef in the informal sense of muscle and physical strength is a synonym of muscularity.

clue.text: Start to hold forth about one spirit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the speech word wraps the rest

parts.note: to orate is to hold forth in speech
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone begins to speak at length about a single drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise or come into being is to start, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Queen upset losing island rum

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read upwards

parts.note: Dido was the legendary Queen of Carthage

explanation.surface: A queen is upset at losing an island's rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is the old British adjective for strange, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum in informal British use means strange or peculiar.

clue.text: Pull swimmer back downwind

indicators.note: back means the combined pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: to draw is to pull
an eel is a swimmer

explanation.surface: An instruction to haul a swimmer back to shore with the wind behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The side sheltered from or facing away from the wind is the downwind side.

clue.text: Refusal from Berlin to host bike races, golf and fishing

indicators.note: to host means to hold inside, as a host holds guests

parts.note: nein is German for no
the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorcycle race series
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A German refuses to stage motorcycle racing, golf and angling events.
explanation.definitionFit: Catching fish with nets is a form of fishing; the gerund matches the gerund.
